findings.reason: the node would be dispatched to produce a count from a source that cannot contain it, and would either fabricate the figure or discover mid-build that the measure §16 could not take is equally untakeable here, which is precisely the gap this clause was added to close.
findings.text: §11 says the census "reclassifies each event through `ticker.stream_carries` and `ticker._pane_word`" and now counts "`review-missing` duties published while a review run standing for that run was live", keeping "the pointer and snapshot lines behind each instance"; but `review-missing` is an obligations duty kind derived at collection time (reckon/crew/obligations.py:1009), never written to the watch stream the census reads, and the snapshot/pointer evidence behind it is what §16's own close comment (c-close-s16, 2026-10-26T21:05Z) records as gone — the pointer is removed at completion and the per-session snapshot is overwritten in place — so a census over a past 24-hour window has neither the event nor the evidence to count

findings.reason: a measure added to the intro but absent from the done-when is not gated, so a census that silently never counts that kind would pass the node's gate.
findings.text: the done-when's report sentence still enumerates only the four pre-existing figures ("zero carried halted rows with `process_alive: true`, zero halted rows returning to working with no new attempt claim, at most one `lift-granted` per lift id, and zero same-word wait rows") and the negative control reproduces only §1's 24 halted rows, so the newly added `review-missing` count has no expected value and no arm that could show the instrument counts it

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `scripts/census/death_census.py` and `carryover_census.py` exist, `ticker.stream_carries` (ticker.py:1363) and `ticker._pane_word` (ticker.py:1346) resolve, §1's table (line 51) does carry "24 rows with `process_alive: true`", and the evidence archive resolves.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the report figures §11's done-when enumerates do not include the newly added `review-missing` count, so the clause the change introduced is not measured by the node's own gate.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the script, its test and the evidence fragment under `docs/evidence/fragments/a-live-worker-is-never-drawn-halted/` are durable repository paths, and the archive `docs/evidence/archive/a-live-worker-is-never-drawn-halted-landed.html` exists.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers reach the script or its symbols; `<node-id>` is a runtime path placeholder, not a plan label.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §11 now counts `review-missing` duties published while a review run was live, but that duty is not a watch-stream event and its evidence is the exact record §16 closed as not retained.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §11 still names one deliverable, one census module plus its co-located test and report; the added `review-missing` count is a second measure inside the same instrument, not a second goal.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §11's only ordering constraint ("re-run once §2–§10 have landed", and §12 records "§11 runs last") resolves to nodes that exist and are all earlier in the plan than §11.
